preflightVisual.comparacion: N1 muestra gesto decisivo con Nexa mirando su obra, profundidad y lecho claro; N2 muestra decisión sobre vidrio con luz de hora dorada y lecho oscuro. Los dos recientes usan un panel de set y proyección en muro. Esta escena cambia a exterior real y mecanismo de medios; la pantalla contiene obra fotográfica con materia y azul propio, no un campo plano ni utilería de estudio.
preflightVisual.oficio: Media & Distribution: revisión de legibilidad y reflejos de una superficie de medio exterior en terreno, sin atribución a cliente.
preflightVisual.azul: El azul activo vive en la fotografía real reproducida por el medio: un toldo arquitectónico azul bajo el cual cruza una persona, con textura y luz del lugar; un reflejo leve sobre el vidrio le da continuidad. No es un rectángulo liso de calibración.
preflightVisual.acento: Un pequeño destello de la luz ámbar anaranjada de un vehículo en movimiento cruza la escena, propio de la calle y no agregado como utilería; no lima.
preflightVisual.lecho: El marco oscuro de la ventana de un vehículo cercano atraviesa el borde inferior, muy próximo al lente y desenfocado; no es una banda inventada.
preflightVisual.identidadVestuario: Rostro, cejas y cabello ondulado de Nexa según las tres referencias canónicas. Camisa marfil y sobrecamisa de arena pálida, pantalón carbón; sin prendas azules o logos.

escena: SCENE (Efeonce Media & Distribution location check in a contemporary Santiago street, clear late-afternoon sun): Nexa is the ONLY recognizable person, photographed candidly in three-quarter profile while she takes one careful step to the side and raises a small unbranded handheld light meter toward an unbranded digital outdoor-media display inside a real glass transit shelter. She is checking whether late sun glare hides the artwork, a real operational decision, not posing or holding a product for the camera. The display shows an actual TEXT-FREE DOCUMENTARY PHOTOGRAPH IN FULL-SCREEN PLAYBACK: one person walks beneath a vivid AZURE BLUE (#0375DB) architectural canopy on an otherwise warm-neutral Santiago sidewalk. Real photographic grain, depth, people-scale, sunlight and shadow are clearly visible INSIDE the displayed photo; the blue belongs to the photographed architecture rather than a flat color rectangle or calibration screen. The image is practical unbranded creative being tested in a real media placement. Its narrow blue reflection on the shelter's side glass continues the same hue into a second depth plane. No plain solid-color display, no empty color block. A moving city bus passes behind her and a tiny natural AMBER-ORANGE (#F55D01) turn-signal glint catches on its brushed metal at the decisive instant; orange is small and functional, with no other saturated accents and no lime. Nexa wears an ivory cotton shirt under a pale warm-sand overshirt and charcoal trousers, no blue or navy garments. Her hair is long, dark and wavy; face and defined brows exactly match the references. She looks at the shelter display and meter, never the camera. Long-lens street photograph, 135mm f/2.8 from across the curb at face height; her face, meter hand and edge of the installation are sharp, passing street movement softly blurred. A strong directional shaft of neutral-warm late sun catches her cheek and the shelter frame, while a crisp real architectural shadow creates graphic geometry away from her face. THREE depth planes: optically blurred dark window frame of a near unbranded vehicle at the very bottom, Nexa and light meter sharp, transit shelter and passing bus behind. Space and clothing clean and cared-for. No readable text, letters, numbers, logos, brand names, watermarks or UI anywhere.

lecho.objeto: the genuinely dark charcoal lower window frame of an unbranded vehicle immediately beside the photographer, a real nearby street surface beneath the sightline to Nexa and the transit shelter
lecho.tono: DARK near black, textured charcoal vehicle interior material in neutral shade, never a featureless graphic slab
